command: OPENREVIEW_GATEWAY__MODELS__GROUNDING__PRIMARY=openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct uv run python scripts/measure_slm_slots.py --grounding-accuracy --arm cloud --limit 20 --corpus-dir corpus --out results/openweight-grounding-70b.json
benchmark_input: corpus assembled inside CI from the repository's tracked fixtures: 96 clause units from 17 documents (tests/fixtures/**/*.txt verbatim plus fixture PDFs/DOCX parsed with openreview_cli.parsing). The CUAD corpus under data/legalbenchrag/ is not used for this run.
notes: Recorded git_commit 42fdf38 is the branch base the measurement actually ran against (the tree is unchanged since); the receipt is committed later, so the recorded commit is deliberately the base and stays an ancestor of main. The grounding slot was reached through a hosted OpenRouter endpoint; a self-hosted run of the same weights would differ in quantization and serving, so these figures are endpoint-specific. Corpus and items: the 96-unit corpus assembled from the repository's tracked fixtures (17 documents) was used at --limit 20, giving 25 known-good positives and 44 planted-bad negatives over 69 scored calls. The positives are each unit's own qualifying sentence plus a narrow, meaning-preserving rewrite, so both positive classes are supported by the clause by construction and only the bad-claim arm discriminates; no real-world false-positive rate may be quoted from it. unreadable_answers counts answers the answer parser could not decode, which separates a parsing defect from model hesitation. This is a single sample of a non-deterministic model, not a benchmark. Exact model id: openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct. Gateway cost ledger (cost_logs) for this model on the run date: 73 calls / 73 cents; the four ladder runs totalled 292 cents.
